events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven pier: rate 1 (below average). Go here.** It is the only pier with a recent report that says what worked: casting spoons or body baits.
- **St. Joseph pier: rate 1 (below average).** Slow, with a few coho on spawn and on spoons or spinners.
- **South Haven pier: rate 1 (below average), with an access caveat.** Its latest pier report only covers the time "when the piers were open."
- **Muskegon pier: rate 1 or lower (my estimate).** There is no 2024 pier report, so this rating is an inference from boat reports.
- For any pier, fish casting spoons or body baits, and expect few fish.

## Why

- Grand Haven gets the nod because its most recent pier report says casting spoons or body baits did better than spawn (Grand Haven, 2024-04-24).
- I'd expect all four piers to stay near 1 this week, since every 2024 pier report is rated slow to below average and the water is only about 47-48 F (Apr 17 and Apr 24 reports, all ports).
- I'd expect the piers to stay slow because past seasons at similar water temperature show pier fishing rated slow or below average (past seasons, Grand Haven and South Haven, May 2023 and May 2022).

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2024-04-24, six days old)
- Grand Haven, 2024-04-24: "Pier anglers caught a few coho salmon and brown trout when casting body baits or spoons." Quality 1. "Anglers reported that casting spoons or body baits seemed to be more productive than using spawn."
- St. Joseph, 2024-04-24: "Pier fishing was on the slow side for all species, but anglers did catch a few coho salmon and steelhead." Quality 1. Fish were caught on spawn and on casting spoons and spinners.
- South Haven, 2024-04-24: "When the piers were open, a few steelhead and coho salmon were caught using spawn." Quality 1.
- Grand Haven, 2024-04-10: pier coho on spawn, quality 1.
- Muskegon: the 2024 reports cover only boats. Boat trolling on 2024-04-10 was "hit or miss" (quality 1).
- Boat results were slightly better than the piers. Grand Haven boats trolling to 50 ft were rated 3 on 2024-04-10, and boats in 25-50 ft were rated 1 on 2024-04-24. The reports do not say the piers were any better than the boats.

**Past seasons** (history, not current conditions)
- With surface water near 48 F, similar weeks in past years had pier results of 0 to 1. Examples: Grand Haven 2023-05-10 (slow, 0), South Haven 2023-05-17 (slow, 0), Grand Haven 2022-05-18 (below average, 1), St. Joseph 2022-05-04 (below average, 1).

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water for the week before 2024-04-30 was 48 F at St. Joseph and South Haven, and 47 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon. Each rose 3 F over the week (buoy, measured).
- The sharp drop that signals upwelling did not show up in this week's buoy data.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from 2024-04-24, six days old. Conditions may have changed since.
- Live conditions were unavailable. The tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2024-04-30. There is no modeled pierhead water temperature or wind forecast, so I could not check for upwelling at the piers.
- Muskegon has no 2024 pier report, so its rating is my inference.
- South Haven's pier access depends on whether the piers are open, and the latest report does not say.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, St. Joseph, South Haven, Muskegon bulletin, 2024-04-24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3987c22
- Bulletin, 2024-04-17: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/39703c8
- Bulletin, 2024-04-10: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/39595be
- Bulletin, 2024-04-03: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/39420c4
